chunks.label: Where you're from
chunks.rationale: Ask and answer where someone comes from.
chunks.interference: Doko kara kita no? usually means which country; shusshin doko? means where you grew up.

chunks.label: Where you live
chunks.rationale: Say where you live and who with.
chunks.interference: Sumu takes ni, not de, and stays in the -te iru form (sunderu).

chunks.label: Your work
chunks.rationale: Ask about someone's job and describe your own.
chunks.interference: Hataraku takes de for the place, while sumu takes ni.

chunks.label: Learning Japanese
chunks.rationale: Talk about your Japanese and keep the conversation in it.
chunks.interference: Hanaseru (can speak) and hanasou (let's speak) differ only in the ending.
members: 日本語勉強してるんだ
日本語どこで勉強したの？

chunks.label: Time in Japan
chunks.rationale: Say how long you've been here and how long you're staying.
chunks.interference: Dono gurai asks how long so far; itsu made asks until when.
members: 日本に来てどのぐらい？

chunks.label: Hobbies and likes
chunks.rationale: Ask about hobbies and say what you like doing.
chunks.interference: Suki takes ga, not o, and a verb needs no before ga.
members: 趣味っていうほどじゃないけど

chunks.label: Your family
chunks.rationale: Ask about brothers and sisters and say who's in your family.
chunks.interference: Your own family words (ani) differ from someone else's (oniisan).

chunks.label: Partner, kids and pets
chunks.rationale: Ask whether someone is married, has kids or keeps pets.
chunks.interference: Kau (keep a pet) sounds the same as kau (buy).

chunks.label: Meeting new people
chunks.rationale: Greet a friend's friend warmly and swap contacts.
chunks.interference: Aete ureshii is warm and personal; a plain first meeting starts with hajimemashite.

chunks.label: Food and drink
chunks.rationale: Talk about food you like, cooking and drinking.
chunks.interference: Nandemo (anything) vs nanimo (nothing, with a negative).

chunks.label: Free time at home
chunks.rationale: Say what you do with free time and ask about films and games.
chunks.interference: Eiga o miru is watching a film; eiga ni iku is going to the cinema.

chunks.label: Places you've been
chunks.rationale: Ask where people have been and say where you'd like to go.
chunks.interference: Itta koto aru? means 'ever been'; itta? asks about one trip.

chunks.label: Why you came
chunks.rationale: Explain why you came to Japan and what got you into something.
chunks.interference: Kikkake is the trigger or starting point; riyuu is the reason.
members: ずっと日本に来たかったんだ

chunks.label: Life in Japan
chunks.rationale: Answer the usual questions about how you're finding Japan.
chunks.interference: Doko ga suki? means 'what do you like about it', not 'which place'.

chunks.label: Music and gigs
chunks.rationale: Talk about the music you like and going to shows.
chunks.interference: Kiku means both 'listen' and 'ask'.
members: 好きなアーティストいる？
洋楽と邦楽どっち聴く？

chunks.label: Sport and exercise
chunks.rationale: Talk about sports and activities you do now or used to do.
chunks.interference: Kayou is going somewhere regularly; iku is a single trip.
members: 何かスポーツやってる？
どのぐらいやってるの？

chunks.label: Taking an interest
chunks.rationale: React to someone's hobby, play down your own, and recommend things.
chunks.interference: Heta (bad at) vs jouzu (good at); don't call yourself jouzu.

chunks.label: Studies and job hunting
chunks.rationale: Say what you study or that you're between jobs.
chunks.interference: None.

chunks.label: Age and blood type
chunks.rationale: Find out someone's age, or their blood type as an icebreaker.
chunks.interference: Nansai? is mostly for children; adults get toshi ikutsu? or oikutsu desu ka?

chunks.label: Describing your hometown
chunks.rationale: Describe where you grew up and where you've lived since.
chunks.interference: None.
